entities.summary: Francesco Carbone Tomacelli was an Italian cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Great Western Schism. Born into a prominent papal family, he became Pope Boniface IX's nephew and a key figure in the schism, which lasted from 1378 to 1417. Tomacelli's influence extended beyond the Vatican, as he collaborated with other European monarchs and clergy to navigate the tumultuous political landscape of the late Middle Ages. His legacy is still felt today, with historians continuing to study the schism and its impact on the development of Western Christianity. The schism, in turn, had far-reaching consequences for the Catholic Church, European politics, and the rise of nation-states. In the end, Tomacelli's influence was tempered by his own mortality, as he died in 1405-06-27, leaving behind a complex and contested legacy that continues to fascinate scholars and historians.
